title: Base change of modules in stages
statement: Let $R\to S\to T$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings and $M$ an $R$-module. Then there is an isomorphism of $T$-modules $(M\otimes_RS)\otimes_ST\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_RT$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $(m\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto m\otimes st$, with inverse $m\otimes t\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes t$. It is natural: for an $R$-linear map $\varphi:M\to M'$ it carries $(\varphi\otimes1_S)\otimes1_T$ to $\varphi\otimes1_T$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule, line 1881): $(M\otimes_AN)\otimes_BP\cong M\otimes_A(N\otimes_BP)$, here with $A=R$, the $(R,S)$-bimodule $N=S$, $P=T$ and $S\otimes_ST=T$; naturality from the formula on generators
